reason: In floras, 'moderately thick' describes a thick part (for example, thick leathery leaves). 'Moderately' only says how strong it is, like 'spinously' in the accepted rule R1901 for spinously muricate. PATO has no mid-range thickness value, and increased thickness already has the synonym 'thickened'.

'Perigonial' is an adjective that needs its noun (perigonial leaves, bracts or buds). On its own it does not say that a perigonial bract (PO_0030028) is present. The part should come from the noun as the bearer.

A protonemal rhizoid (PO_0030079) is wrong. 'Protonematous' usually describes gemmae, flagella or rhizoids that are protonema-like, or a persistent protonema. Retargeting to protonema (PO_0030003) present would be either always true for mosses or the wrong meaning. It is ambiguous, so no rule.
'Rhizoautoicous' is a spelling of rhizautoicous. FLOPO_0991295 exists, is a child of autoicous (FLOPO_0991093), and its definition matches: male shoots connected to the female stem only by rhizoids.

This is a part plus a quality: the leaf bases have broken up into fibres. Saying only that a leaf base (PO_0020040) is present loses the point. It needs leaf base as the bearer with a fibrous or shredded quality, not a word rule.

In bryophyte descriptions, 'spiculate-papillate' means a surface with papillae that end in a fine point. The surface really is papillose, and 'spiculate' only describes the papillae, like R1901 spinously muricate.

Strumate is the same as strumose (a struma is a one-sided swelling, usually at the base of a moss capsule). The rule for strumose (R0283) was already reviewed and maps it to gibbous. Keep this one the same way.
'Traces of fibrils' means that only a few fibrils remain. Fibrillary (PATO_0002134) says the structure is fibrous. No existing class means 'faintly or vestigially fibrillose'.
'Tolerant to' (PATO_0000515) is a relation and needs the thing tolerated. Without salt the statement is empty. This needs a pattern with salt as the object, or a halophyte or salt-tolerant class.

These are two separate qualities: the covering is white (colour) and mealy (PATO_0104364, texture). One rule to mealy throws the colour statement away. The word should be split into white + mealy, not mapped to one class.
Laxiflorous means the flowers are loosely arranged, which makes the inflorescence loose (PATO_0001802). It does not fit leaves, stems or other parts.

In floras, a 'tendril-terminated' leaf is mostly a pinnate leaf whose rachis ends in a tendril (PO_0025366). Inflorescences and branches have other tendril classes (PO_0025364, PO_0025365). Simple leaves that end in a tendril (Gloriosa, Flagellaria) would be leaf apex tendril (PO_0025363), which is a small leftover risk.

Tigré means marked with stripes or spots of another colour. Banded/striped (PATO_0001946) would be wrong for the spotted sense. Multi-colored (synonym variegated) is a true, safe parent class of both.
Velutinous means covered in dense, short, soft hairs, which is the velvety kind of tomentum. 'Velvety-tomentose' describes the same cover, so it is not two separate qualities.
'Battened' is not a botanical word for buttressed (FLOPO_0991138), and no source links them. It is probably a bad translation. The meaning is unclear.

Brachystylous names the short-styled morph of a flower, not the heterostylous condition of the species (FLOPO_0991137). Descriptions often contrast brachystylous and dolichostylous flowers, so both words would collapse into one class. It needs a morph class, for example a child of distylous (FLOPO_0991260).
Brown and mottled are two separate qualities: colour, and a pattern (PATO_0002274). One rule loses the colour. The word should be split into brown + mottled.

'Ciliate-fringed' means fringed with fine marginal hairs, which is ciliate. In the flora union pairs, PATO_0001408 is already the grounding for ciliate, and ciliate and fimbriate are treated as different alternatives (pair 125).

Emerging means exserted (PATO_0000623) for parts that stick out of a surrounding part, such as stamens from a corolla or a capsule from its bracts. For leaves, shoots or seedlings it means newly appearing.

Flared (PATO_0040022) fits tube-like parts that gradually widen towards the mouth. For leaf blades and bracts it describes an outline shape, and for petioles it describes widening into a sheath, so those parts are left out.
Independent means free (FLOPO_0991068, not fused) only for parts that are sometimes fused with each other. Elsewhere, for example a plant or a branch, it has another meaning.
Secondary leaf vein (PO_0020140) only fits leaves and leaflets. Lateral nerves of bracts, sepals or petals are not leaf veins.
'Light' only gives the shade of the same colour, and PATO has no light chestnut. The plain chestnut colour is a true parent class, like keeping 'muricate' for spinously muricate (R1901).
Mamillated is a spelling of mammillate. FLOPO_0991217 already exists for nipple-shaped protuberances, and its definition sets it apart from tubercles and papillae.

This is a quality plus a place. 'At base' is already a region context word (config/flora_context_words.tsv), so the base becomes the bearer. A whole-phrase rule to tapered would bypass that step and put the quality on the whole organ.
French 'obtus-arrondi' means blunt and rounded, a single apex shape. PATO obtuse already has the synonym 'roundish', so nothing important is lost.
This is connate (FLOPO_0991067) plus a place. 'At base' is a region context word, so the base becomes the bearer. A whole-phrase rule would wrongly say the parts are fused along their whole length.
Circumferential (running around the circumference, as in a circumferential slit, ring or dehiscence line) is not surrounding another structure (PATO_0001772). No existing class fits all its uses.
'Flattenuated' is not a botanical word. It may be a typo for flattened or attenuated, or a blend of the two. Since we cannot tell which, no rule.

'Smelly' says that a smell is present, not that it is foul. Odorous (PATO_0001331) is the value class and the parent of foetid (FLOPO_0991020). It is better than the attribute 'odor' (PATO_0000058) that the first check suggested.
